newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's unemployment falls to 9.4 pct in Aug.
newsitem.headline: Canada's unemployment falls to 9.4 pct in Aug.

text.p: - Statistics Canada said on Friday the unemployment rate fell to 9.4 percent in August from 9.8 percent in July.
Employment growth was the fastest in three years.
Note - Labor force, employment and unemployment in millions, on seasonally adjusted basis.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the unemployment rate to drop to 9.7 percent and employment to grow by 26,000 in August.
Full-time employment rose by 75,000 from the month before, after a 37,000 gain in July, wiping out recent full-time job losses.
Part-time employment rose by 7,000 after falling 18,000 in July. The 82,000 rise in employment was the largest since an 88,000 gain in June 1993, Statistics Canada said.
The overall unemployment rate returned to the same level as May, a level around which it had long hovered before June's sharp rise to 10.0 percent.

Prime Minister Jean Chretien had characterized the June spike as a "blip" and declined to embark on any emergency measures to rescue jobs, continuing to rely instead mainly on falling interest rates stemming from lower budget deficits.

Unemployment in Quebec, which is run by a separatist government, fell to 11.8 percent in August from 12.4 percent in July, as employment rose 41,000, only partly offsetting the estimated loss of 76,000 jobs in June and July.
Employment in Quebec is still down 17,000 from the beginning of the year, although up 5,000 from a year ago.
For the year to date, 153,000 jobs have been created in Canada. Statistics Canada said the job creation in August more than offset the job losses in June.

Manufacturing employment rose for the second consecutive month, by 41,000 or two percent, consistent with second- quarter gains in merchandise exports. Construction jobs also rose, in line with second-quarter growth in housing starts.
Public sector jobs rose marginally, but have shown an overall loss of 46,000 since the beginning of the year.
